clue.text: Islander, terrible hypocrite, he ignored

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word before them

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone from an island has a terrible hypocrite in their midst, and he was ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H and E out of HYPOCRITE, leaving YPOCRIT, then rearrange to CYPRIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cypriot is a native of Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Happy to salute youth leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to cheer someone is to salute or hail them
the opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to greet the leader of a youth group.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheery is a synonym of happy, describing a bright, cheerful mood.

clue.text: Doorman admitting characteristic bore, an artist

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first word takes the following words inside it

blocks.note: a porter guards the door of a building
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
a tiresome person or thing is a pain or a bore

explanation.surface: A doorman lets in a dull, typical bore who turns out to be an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the characteristic and the bore go inside the doorman together, splitting him after his third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait painter is one kind of artist, specialising in likenesses of people.

clue.text: Brown is one of its members, girl with class

definitions.text: Brown is one of its members

blocks.note: Ivy is a girl's name
to be in a different league is to be in a different class

explanation.surface: A girl with class: Brown, it seems, is a member of her circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a surname or a colour; it is Brown University in Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is a group of eight elite US universities, of which Brown University is one.

clue.text: Whippet finally spots litter

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the closing letter of whippet
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A whippet at last sees some rubbish lying about.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish, the same thing as litter dropped in the street.

clue.text: Hit rain when high, and this on Everest?

definitions.text: Hit rain when high, and this on Everest?

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber high on Everest gets hit by rain and finds the atmosphere scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition: at great height on Everest the air is thin, and that is where rain would hit you.
explanation.definitionFit: The rarefied atmosphere at extreme altitude is literally thin air, with little oxygen to breathe.

clue.text: Go mad, disconcert a worthy

blocks.note: to throw someone is to disconcert them
taken as written
fit means worthy or suitable, as in fit for a king

explanation.surface: Lose your temper and upset some respected local worthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a fit is an idiom for losing one's temper violently.

clue.text: Wrongdoer beheaded in secret

indicators.note: a beheaded word has lost its head, meaning its opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a sinner is one who does wrong

explanation.surface: A criminal is executed in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNER loses its S to leave INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings or thoughts are private ones, kept hidden and so secret.

clue.text: A card game, distraction not including one shorter form

indicators.note: not including something means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game for four players
a diversion is something that distracts attention
the Roman numeral for one; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A game of cards is a diversion, though one that is excluded here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the Roman numeral I, and it is the distraction word that loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged version of a text is a condensed edition, cut down from the original.

clue.text: Revolutionary annoyed relief organisation

blocks.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries and communists
cross means angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: A radical is irritated by an aid agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international humanitarian body that provides disaster and medical aid.

clue.text: Forward almost missing header

indicators.note: a word missing its header has lost the letter at its head, its very first

blocks.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A football striker nearly scores but misses with a header.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward and header suggest football; NEARLY loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward can mean premature or advanced for the time, as in a forward spring, which is early.

clue.text: Plant from Andorra, so peculiar

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are put into an odd new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant comes from Andorra, so it is rather unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a common name for great mullein and other tall flowering herbs, after the biblical rod that blossomed.

clue.text: Carnival uncommon around the East at present

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word goes about the next one

blocks.note: rare means uncommon
E is the abbreviation for east
to present something is to show it

explanation.surface: A carnival from the East is an unusual sight at present.
explanation.walkthrough: The East letter sits inside the word for uncommon just before its last letter; 'at' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree show is an old travelling street spectacle or peep show, the kind of entertainment seen at a fair or carnival.

clue.text: Attacker overlooking a person on a horse

indicators.note: overlooking something means missing it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a raider is one who attacks
taken as written; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An assailant looks down on a horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface but belongs to the wordplay: RAIDER without its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone mounted on and controlling a horse.

clue.text: Settlers introducing dour priest to lager-like beer

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another means putting it inside, so the following words go into the beer

blocks.note: Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager-style beer
grim means stern or dour
Father is the title of a Catholic priest

explanation.surface: Colonists offer a stern clergyman his first taste of pale beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pils, short for Pilsner, is opened up after its third letter to take in the dour priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers were the English colonists who sailed on the Mayflower and founded Plymouth Colony in 1620.

clue.text: The very same dialect in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The same local dialect is heard at the holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday town; it is re-sort, an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, one and the same thing.

clue.text: Start to trust man brought in to handle as much as possible

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept
brought in means placed inside, so these letters go into the words that follow

blocks.note: the opening letter of trust
he is the pronoun for a man
to taken as written, then a hilt is the handle of a sword

explanation.surface: To build trust, a new man is hired to take on as much work as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'to's: the first belongs to the start indicator, the second is kept as written in front of the handle.
explanation.definitionFit: To the hilt is an idiom meaning completely, from a blade driven in right up to its handle.

clue.text: Crazy shot leading cup

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first word comes before the second

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to have a shot at it
a pot is a trophy cup in sporting slang

explanation.surface: A wild shot puts a team in front in the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot means eccentric or mad, used of people and their wild ideas.

clue.text: Typical delegate

blocks.note: first meaning: characteristic of a class, as an example of it
second meaning: a person chosen to act or speak for others

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like an ordinary delegate; the two words are separate meanings, one adjective and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something serving as an example and a noun for an agent acting on behalf of others.

clue.text: Briefly set out American position

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to state something is to set it out
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American position is set out in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' shortens only the word for set out, not the American part.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank, one's position in society.

clue.text: Fresh Police Constable arresting male teacher, retired

indicators.note: arresting someone means holding them, so the policeman holds the next word inside
retired means went back, so the whole combination is read backwards

blocks.note: PC is the standard abbreviation
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A cheeky constable arrests a retired schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp means fresh and firm, like crisp lettuce or a crisp morning.

clue.text: Recently stolen - that appears in Post Office picture

indicators.note: what appears in something is seen within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
hot goods are stolen ones, still too risky to sell

explanation.surface: A stolen item turns up pictured at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Hush-hush operation with leading character in Coronation Street amazingly being brought round

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its first letter, the only one kept
amazingly suggests something turned about in astonishing fashion, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: op is short for operation
the opening letter of Coronation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret operation in the TV soap Coronation Street brings a character round.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap opera set in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush is informal for confidential, so top secret at the highest level.

clue.text: Quietly press for expulsion

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
to urge is to press someone to act

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly lobbies to have a person thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is the removal of unwanted members from a party or organisation, an expulsion.

clue.text: Police vehicle part modified by Carlo abroad

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so its letters are reordered
abroad means astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Part of a police car has been modified by an Italian called Carlo overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol car is a police car that cruises an area to keep watch.

clue.text: I spot one inside supplying dope

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the numeral goes into the word for spot

blocks.note: taken as written
a dot is a small spot
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a person inside who is dealing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope looks like drugs, in keeping with supplying; here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is informal for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Industry importing special rum, a racket

indicators.note: special suggests a made-to-order version, so the letters are rearranged into a new form
importing means bringing in, so the first word takes the next inside it

blocks.note: industry in the sense of hard work, toil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business brings in a special rum as part of a smuggling racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Industry and importing suggest trade; industry here is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is uproar and confusion, and racket can mean a din or commotion.

clue.text: Reaches former nurses

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to tend the sick is to nurse them

explanation.surface: Someone gets in touch with nurses they used to work with.
explanation.definitionFit: Extends and reaches both mean stretches out as far as a point.
